_comment: Awareness and Training Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with PS (PS-6 access agreements paired with AT-2 awareness training; PS-9 position descriptions cite AT-3 role-based requirements), IR (AT-2(3) phishing exercises produce reports that flow into IR), SA (SA-3 SDLC integration depends on AT-3 developer training), and PE (PE-3 / PE-6 implicate visitor-escort and physical-security awareness). Smallest 800-53 family — 4 base controls + 2 in-baseline enhancements at moderate; the rigor is in role-based curriculum design and completion-tracking discipline.
title: Awareness and Training Plan
description: Documents how the system's user, administrator, and developer populations are trained in security awareness, role-based duties, insider-threat indicators, social-engineering / phishing recognition, and how training records are maintained. Covers the controls of the AT family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-50 (Building an Information Technology Security Awareness and Training Program), NIST SP 800-181 r1 (NICE Workforce Framework), DoD 8140.03 (Cyberspace Workforce Qualification and Management), and Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) annual training requirements.
intro_template:
This Awareness and Training Plan documents the awareness and training approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, curriculum, cadences, and roles used to deliver baseline security-literacy training, role-based training tailored to specific responsibilities, insider-threat awareness, social-engineering / phishing recognition, and the recordkeeping that demonstrates compliance.

The scope covers literacy training and awareness per AT-2 (with insider-threat and social-engineering enhancements where applicable), role-based training per AT-3, and training records per AT-4 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Awareness and Training family), NIST SP 800-50 / SP 800-16 r1 (training program guidance), and NIST SP 800-181 r1 (NICE Workforce Framework).
approach_function:
{system_name} delivers baseline security awareness training through {lms_platform} on the cadence in §4.2. Role-based training (AT-3) is mapped to position-description responsibilities per §4.5. Insider-threat awareness (AT-2(2)) is delivered via {insider_threat_program_link}. Phishing-simulation exercises (AT-2(3)) are run by {phishing_program_role} on the cadence in §4.4. Training records are maintained in {training_record_system} and reconciled with the access-list (AC-2 / PE-2) on the cadence in §6.

Additional details on literacy and awareness, insider-threat awareness, social-engineering exercises, role-based training, and training records are captured in the sub-sections below.

continuous_monitoring_template: Awareness-and-training performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (annual literacy-training completion rate, role-based-training completion rate, phishing-simulation click-rate trend, phishing-report rate, insider-threat-awareness completion rate, time-from-onboarding-to-first-training-completed, training-record-currency rate). The training roster is reconciled with the personnel roster on the cadence in §6.2; access (AC-2 / PE-2) is conditioned on training currency, with overdue-training auto-suspension as the enforcement mechanism. Phishing-simulation results feed both AT and IR processes — patterns surfaced in simulation drive curriculum updates and inform IR detection-rule tuning.
integration_template: This Awareness and Training Plan does not stand alone. The PS family pairs PS-6 access agreements with AT-2 awareness training; PS-9 position descriptions cite AT-3 role-based training requirements. The IR family receives reports from AT-2(3) phishing simulations as a detection feed; insider-threat indicators from AT-2(2) escalate via the same path. The SA family depends on AT-3 developer training to underwrite SA-3 SDLC integration. The PE family delivers visitor-escort and physical-security awareness through this plan's curriculum. The CA family validates AT outcomes via CA-2 assessment of training effectiveness. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where AT-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Enterprise security-awareness program (when shared LMS + curriculum)

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Platforms and roles that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: LMS / training platform (one-liner)
questions.help: Where awareness + role-based training is delivered (e.g., 'KnowBe4 (commercial)', 'DoD CyberAwareness Challenge via JKO', 'Internal Moodle deployment with SCORM courses').

questions.label: Training-record system (one-liner)
questions.help: Authoritative system for training records (often the LMS itself, or a separate HRMS module that aggregates LMS + classroom + external).

questions.label: Insider-threat program reference
questions.help: Pointer to the org's insider-threat program — typically CISA-aligned for federal. Reference for AT-2(2) coordination.

questions.label: Phishing-simulation program owner role
questions.help: Role accountable for phishing simulations (e.g., 'Security Awareness Lead under CISO', 'Enterprise SOC Phishing Operations').

questions.label: Training-program lead role
questions.help: Senior role accountable for the awareness-and-training program (often Chief Learning Officer / CISO delegate).

questions.label: Annual training cadence summary
questions.help: One-line summary of annual cadence (e.g., 'AT-2 baseline annually + on initial onboarding; AT-3 role-based at hire + annually + on role change'). Detail goes in the dedicated sub-section.

family_questions.label: Literacy Training and Awareness (AT-2)
family_questions.description: Baseline security training that all users receive.

questions.label: Baseline curriculum topics
options: Acceptable use policy + Rules of Behavior

questions.label: Delivery cadence (AT-2 ODV)
questions.help: When training is delivered (e.g., 'Within 5 business days of onboarding; annually thereafter; within 30 days of role change'). AT-2 ODV.

questions.label: Completion criteria
questions.help: What counts as 'complete' (e.g., 'Module completion + 80% on knowledge check; failed attempt → retake').

questions.label: Program-content review cadence
questions.help: How often the awareness curriculum is reviewed for currency (typical: 'Annually + on regulatory change'). AT-2 ODV.

questions.label: Event-triggered updates (AT-2(1))
questions.help: Per AT-2(1) — content updates triggered by significant events (incident affecting org, new threat, regulatory change). Even though AT-2(1) may not be in moderate baseline, this is good practice.

family_questions.label: Insider-Threat Awareness (AT-2(2))
family_questions.description: Per AT-2(2), training on indicators and reporting paths.

questions.label: In-scope audience for AT-2(2)
options: Personnel with access to critical components (RA-9)

questions.label: Reporting path
questions.help: How an observer reports a concern (anonymous hotline, ISSO direct, EAP-assisted referral). Reference org insider-threat program contact.

questions.label: Protections for reporters
questions.help: Anti-retaliation policy, anonymity preservation. Reference org whistleblower policy.

family_questions.label: Social-Engineering and Phishing (AT-2(3))
family_questions.description: Per AT-2(3), training plus simulated exercises.

questions.label: Phishing-simulation cadence
questions.help: How often phishing simulations are run (e.g., 'Quarterly broad-cast; monthly targeted'). AT-2(3) ODV.

questions.label: Simulation difficulty progression
questions.help: How simulation difficulty escalates over time (e.g., 'Easy generic in Q1; spear-phishing tied to system context in Q3; voice-phishing exercises annually').

questions.label: Response to simulation failure
questions.help: What happens when a user clicks / enters credentials in a simulation. Just-in-time micro-training, manager notification, repeated-failure escalation. Reference PS-8 only as last resort.

questions.label: User report mechanism
questions.help: How users report suspected phishing in production (e.g., 'PhishAlarm button in Outlook; submitted to SOC for analysis').

questions.label: Click-rate target / phish-report-rate target
questions.help: Targets for the program (e.g., 'Click rate <5%; report rate >40% on simulations within 60 minutes').

family_questions.label: Role-Based Training (AT-3)
family_questions.description: Per AT-3, training tailored to the security responsibilities of each role.

questions.label: Role-taxonomy source
options: Other industry framework (e.g., (ISC)² CISSP body of knowledge)

questions.label: Role-to-curriculum mapping
questions.help: Crosswalk from each role to required training (e.g., 'Privileged users: MIS-525 plus CompTIA Security+; Developers: SSDF familiarization + secure-coding + threat-modeling; Incident responders: SANS FOR-508 or equivalent'). Often summarized as a separate appendix.

questions.label: Delivery cadence (AT-3 ODV)
questions.help: When AT-3 training is delivered (e.g., 'At hire / role assignment; annually thereafter; on significant role expansion'). AT-3 ODV.

questions.label: Certification requirements
questions.help: Roles that require external certification (e.g., 'CISSP for ISSO; Security+ CE for privileged users per DoD 8140; OSCP for red-team members'). Time-to-attain after role start.

questions.label: Continuing-education requirement
questions.help: How CE units are tracked (e.g., '40 hours per role per year; CISSP renewal at 120 CPEs / 3 years').

questions.label: Required record fields
options: Linked role at time of training

questions.label: Record-retention period (AT-4 ODV)
questions.help: How long training records are retained. AT-4 ODV. Common: 'Per NARA records-retention schedule'; 'Length of employment + 5 years'.

questions.label: Record-review cadence
questions.help: How often training records are reviewed for completeness / accuracy (e.g., 'Quarterly reconciliation against personnel roster').

questions.label: Audit-trail requirement
questions.help: How changes to training records are themselves audited (immutable LMS log, separate audit table). Reference AU plan.

family_questions.label: Training Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: Quantitative scope numbers that anchor metrics later in the plan.

questions.label: Total trainees in scope
questions.help: Approximate count of all personnel requiring AT-2 baseline training.

questions.label: Personnel requiring role-based training
questions.help: Approximate count of personnel in AT-3 roles.

questions.label: Distinct AT-3 roles defined
questions.help: Number of distinct role-based training tracks (e.g., '8 — System Owner, ISSO, Privileged User, Developer, IR Analyst, etc.').

questions.label: Phishing-simulation user pool size
questions.help: Approximate count of users targeted in phishing simulations (typically all email-capable personnel).

family_questions.label: Awareness-and-Training Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate AT control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: AT-2 baseline-training completion rate (current vs roster)
AT-2(3) mean time to report (trend down)
Certification currency rate (CE units on track)
Open POA&M items linked to AT controls

family_questions.label: Training-Access Enforcement
family_questions.description: How training currency is tied to access.

questions.label: Enforcement mechanism
options: Auto-suspend access on overdue (typically privileged accounts only)
Manager notification on overdue (warning) + escalation to suspension

questions.label: Grace period before enforcement
questions.help: Days after due date before enforcement action (e.g., '14 days for privileged accounts; 30 days for standard').

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the AT control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.2').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for AT findings
questions.help: Convention for AT-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-AT-' for general).

questions.label: PS handoff
questions.help: How PS-6 access agreements pair with AT-2 awareness training; PS-9 position descriptions cite AT-3 requirements.

questions.label: IR handoff
questions.help: How AT-2(3) phishing-simulation results feed IR detection; insider-threat indicators escalate via the same path.

questions.label: SA handoff
questions.help: How AT-3 developer-training underwrites SA-3 SDLC integration. Where the developer-training catalog lives.

questions.label: PE handoff
questions.help: How AT delivers the visitor-escort and physical-security awareness PE-3 / PE-6 implicate.

questions.label: CA handoff
questions.help: How CA-2 assessments validate AT outcomes (training-effectiveness assessment, knowledge-check sampling, behavioral metrics).

questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying AT continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: Per NIST SP 800-50, activities that focus user attention on security topics. Distinct from training (skill development) and education (broad understanding).
Business Email Compromise — a form of social engineering targeting financial transactions or credential disclosure by impersonating trusted parties. Often mixes phishing with vishing follow-up.
Continuing Education units / Continuing Professional Education credits — units required to maintain certifications. Tracked under AT-3 for personnel holding CISSP / CISA / Security+ / etc.
In phishing simulations, the percentage of recipients who clicked a simulated phishing link. Tracked under AT-2(3) as a leading indicator of awareness program effectiveness.
DoD Manual 8140.03 — Cyberspace Workforce Qualification and Management Program. Mandates training and certification by role for DoD cyberspace personnel.
Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 — federal law requiring agencies to implement information-security programs, including annual training requirements.
A threat to the organization originating from a person with authorized access. Per AT-2(2), training covers indicators of insider activity and reporting paths.
Joint Knowledge Online — DoD's online training delivery platform; common LMS for federal CyberAwareness Challenge delivery.
Learning Management System — the software platform delivering and tracking training (e.g., Moodle, Cornerstone, Saba, KnowBe4).
NIST SP 800-181 r1 — National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education Workforce Framework. Defines a taxonomy of cybersecurity work roles, used for AT-3 role mapping.
Per AT-2(3), a controlled exercise where benign messages are sent to users to measure susceptibility and provide just-in-time training. Distinct from production phishing.
Percentage of phishing-simulation recipients who reported the message via the phish-report button. Tracked as a positive metric — the inverse of click rate.
A social-engineering technique where the attacker fabricates a scenario to manipulate the target into providing information or access. Often a precursor to phishing or vishing.
Per AT-3, training tailored to the security responsibilities of a specific role. Distinct from baseline (AT-2) which applies to all users.
Sharable Content Object Reference Model / Experience API — interoperability standards for e-learning content tracked by an LMS.
SMS-based phishing — a social-engineering attack delivered via text message.
A physical-security violation where one person follows an authorized person through a controlled entry without independent credential verification. Often covered in AT-2 awareness.
Voice-based phishing — a social-engineering attack delivered via phone call.
A targeted phishing attack against high-value individuals (executives, system administrators).
Successor to SCORM — captures broader learning experiences including informal learning and simulations. Common in modern LMS platforms.
